Ari —

Please find our consolidated technical responses below and the evidence pack attached. We focused answers on the items you flagged (transfer safeguards, KMS/keys, logging/audit schema, subprocessor locations, model routing mitigation). For traceability we numbered our responses to match your Section B questions.

Attachments included (zipped): redwood_dpf_evidence_pack_v1.zip 
Inside the ZIP: redwood-export-evidence-summary.pdf, kms_diagram.svg, logging_schema_samples.csv, dpa_annex_fill.pdf

Summary answers (high level):
1) Cross-border legal basis and technical safeguards: We support DPF/SCC alternatives where applicable. For EU→US processing we provide a DPA annex that maps data flows and selects one of the following controls as appropriate: SCCs (standard contractual clauses), binding transfer framework (where customer elects), or detailed technical controls (data minimization + per-request routing). See attached dpa_annex_fill.pdf for clause-level mappings.

2) KMS and key custody: Default hosted deployment uses cloud KMS with envelope encryption; we provide optional HSM-backed key custody for Dedicated/Private deployments. kms_diagram.svg shows key hierarchy: customer data encrypted with per-customer DEKs; DEKs wrapped by KEKs managed in customer-selected KMS (customer-managed key option available). We support Bring-Your-Own-Key via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault and offer HSM integrations for on-prem.

3) Logging / export & audit schema: We log request metadata required for export/audit: request_id, tenant_id, model_id, region_routed, input_hash (truncated), timestamp, action (generate/embedding), response_token_count, routing_decision, cache_hit, and applied_policies. Sample CSV in ZIP shows schema and example entries. Logs are retained per contract (default 90 days) and can be extended. Logs are accessible via secure bucket export or our console with SOC2-compliant access controls.

4) Subprocessor locations and controls: Primary subprocessors (cloud compute, object storage, telemetry) are listed in our subprocessor register. For US/EU splits we maintain EU-located compute pools available for customers requiring residency. Full subprocessor list and country mappings are included in the evidence pack.

5) Model-specific mitigations & routing: We support policy-based routing rules at the customer level. For MediQuell you can pin EU-only model variants; in those cases all inference occurs on EU pools and metadata/logs for those requests are stored in-region. We also support automatic fallback to lower-cost global variants with explicit policy-based consent or on capacity shortage.

6) Timeline and deliverables: This ZIP is the draft evidence set. If you confirm priority questions we will follow up with an annotated DPA annex (completed) and the full subprocessor attestation within 48 business hours.
